options.text: What is this place?

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: This is the Champions' Guild. Only adventurers who have proved themselves worthy by gaining influence from quests are allowed in here.

options.text: Can I have a quest?

steps.player: Can I have a quest?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Aha!

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Yes! A mighty and perilous quest fit only for the most powerful champions! And, at the end of it, you will earn the right to wear the legendary rune platebody!
If the player does not have 45 combat or 33 Magic:
Before starting this quest, be aware that your combat level is lower than the recommended level of 45. One or more of your skill levels are also lower than recommended.

steps.prompt: Start the Dragon Slayer I quest?

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: So, what is this quest?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: You'll have to speak to Oziach, the maker of rune armour. He sets the quests that champions must complete in order to wear it.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Oziach lives in a hut, by the cliffs to the west of Edgeville. He can be a little...odd...sometimes, though.

options.text: No.

steps.player: Actually, I'll give it a miss.

options.text: What is this place?
Can I have a quest?

steps.player: Can I have a quest?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: You're already on a quest for me, if I recall correctly. Have you talked to Oziach yet?

steps.player: No, not yet.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Well, he's the only one who can grant you the right to wear rune platemail. He lives in a hut, by the cliffs west of Edgeville.

steps.player: Okay, I'll go and talk to him.

a-quest-for-the-rune-platebody-talking-t.speaker: Oziach
a-quest-for-the-rune-platebody-talking-t.text: Aye, 'tis a fair day my friend.

options.text: Can you sell me a rune platebody?

steps.player: Can you sell me a rune platebody?

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: So, how does thee know I 'ave some?

options.text: The Guildmaster of the Champions' Guild told me.

steps.player: The Guildmaster of the Champions' Guild told me.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Yes, I suppose he would, wouldn't he? He's always sending you fancy-pants 'heroes' up to bother me. Telling me I'll give them a quest or sommat like that.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Well, I'm not going to let just anyone wear my rune platemail. It's only for heroes. So, leave me alone.

options.text: I thought you were going to give me a quest.

steps.player: I thought you were going to give me a quest.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Sigh*

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: All right, I'll give ye a quest. I'll let ye wear my rune platemail if ye...

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Slay the dragon of Crandor!

options.text: A dragon, that sounds like fun.

steps.player: A dragon, that sounds like fun!

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Hah, yes, you are a typical reckless adventurer, aren't you? Now go kill the dragon and get out of my face.

steps.player: But how can I defeat the dragon?

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Go talk to the Guildmaster in the Champions' Guild. He'll help ye out if yer so keen on doing a quest. I'm not going to be handholding any adventurers.

options.text: I may be a champion, but I don't think I'm up to dragon-killing yet.

steps.player: I may be a champion, but I don't think I'm up to dragon-killing yet.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Yes, I can understand that. Yer a coward.

options.text: That's a pity, I'm not a hero.

steps.player: That's a pity, I'm not a hero.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Aye, I ken tell!

options.text: I am a master detective.

steps.player: I am a master detective.

steps.text: If Murder Mystery has been completed:

steps.player: I solved the Sinclair murder mystery by myself!

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Never 'eard of yer.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Well, however you found out about it, I'm not going to let just anyone wear my rune platemail. It's only for heroes. So leave me alone.

options.text: I thought you were going to give me a quest.
That's a pity, I'm not a hero.
I'm not your friend.
Yes, it's a very nice day.

a-quest-for-the-rune-platebody-talking-t.speaker: Oziach
a-quest-for-the-rune-platebody-talking-t.text: Have ye slayed that dragon yet?

options.text: What is this place?
I talked to Oziach...

steps.player: I talked to Oziach and he gave me a quest.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Oh? What did he tell you to do?

steps.player: Defeat the dragon of Crandor.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: The dragon of Crandor?

steps.player: Um, yes...

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Goodness, he hasn't given you an easy job, has he?

steps.player: What's so special about this dragon?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Thirty years ago, Crandor was a thriving community with a great tradition of mages and adventurers. Many Crandorians even earned the right to be part of the Champions' Guild!

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: One of their adventurers went too far, however. He descended into the volcano in the centre of Crandor and woke the dragon Elvarg.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: He must have fought valiantly against the dragon because they say that, to this day, she has a scar down her side,

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: but the dragon still won the fight. She emerged and laid waste to the whole of Crandor with her fire breath!

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Some refugees managed to escape in fishing boats. They landed on the coast, north of Rimmington, and set up camp but the dragon followed them and burned the camp to the ground.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Out of all the people of Crandor there were only three survivors: a trio of wizards who used magic to escape. Their names were Thalzar, Lozar and Melzar.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: If you're serious about taking on Elvarg, first you'll need to get to Crandor, and to my knowledge, the only way to do that is by sea.

steps.player: So I just sail over there? Seems easy enough.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: If only that were true. The island is surrounded by dangerous underwater reefs. You'll need a map to guide you through them and a ship capable of doing so.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: And then of course there's the dragon herself. Once you reach Crandor, you'll need some kind of protection against her breath.

options.text: Where can I find a map to Crandor?

steps.player: Where can I find a map to Crandor?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: After what happened, people were afraid of enraging the dragon. Most maps to the island were destroyed, but I have heard that one survived. It was held by Melzar, Thalzar and Lozar.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: However, the three apparently split the map into three pieces, which each of them taking one piece.

options.text: Where is Melzar's map piece?

steps.player: Where is Melzar's map piece?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Melzar built a castle on the site of the Crandorian refugee camp, north of Rimmington. He's locked himself in there and no one's seen him for years.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: The inside of his castle is like a maze, and is populated by undead monsters. Maybe, if you could get all the way through the maze, you could find his piece of the map.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Adventurers sometimes go in there to prove themselves, so I can give you this key to Melzar's Maze.
The Guildmaster hands you a key.

options.text: Where is Thalzar's map piece?

steps.player: Where is Thalzar's map piece?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Thalzar was the most paranoid of the three wizards. He hid his map piece and took the secret of its location to his grave.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: I don't think you'd be able to find out where it is by ordinary means. You'll need to talk to the Oracle on Ice Mountain.

options.text: Where is Lozar's map piece?

steps.player: Where is Lozar's map piece?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: A few weeks ago, I'd have told you to speak to Lozar herself, in her house across the river from Lumbridge.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Unfortunately, goblin raiders killed her and stole everything. One of the goblins from the Goblin Village probably has the map piece now.

options.text: What kind of ship do I need?

steps.player: What kind of ship do I need?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Quite a specific one I'm afraid. Even with a map, very few ships will be able to navigate the reefs around the island. You're going to need one of Crandorian design.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: If there's still one in existence, it's probably in Port Sarim. However, a ship will also need a captain, and I'm not sure where you'd find one willing to sail to Crandor!
If the player has completed Pandemonium:

steps.player: Could I not just captain it myself? I have some experience in that area.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: I suppose you could, but given you have a dragon to be dealing with, I'd suggest getting someone else to worry about the captaining for you.

options.text: How can I protect myself from the dragon's breath?

steps.player: How can I protect myself from the dragon's breath?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: That part shouldn't be too difficult, actually. I believe the Duke of Lumbridge has a special shield in his armoury that is enchanted against dragon's breath.

options.text: What's so special about this dragon?
Okay, I'll get going!

steps.player: Okay, I'll get going!

options.text: What is this place?
About my quest to kill the dragon...

steps.player: About my quest to kill the dragon...

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: If you're serious about taking on Elvarg, first you'll need to get to Crandor, and to my knowledge, the only way to do that is by sea.

steps.player: So I just sail over there? Seems easy enough.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: If only that were true. The island is surrounded by dangerous underwater reefs. You'll need a map to guide you through them and a ship capable of doing so.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: And then of course there's the dragon herself. Once you reach Crandor, you'll need some kind of protection against her breath.

options.text: Where can I find a map to Crandor?
What kind of ship do I need?
How can I protect myself from the dragon's breath?
What's so special about this dragon?
Okay, I'll get going!

steps.text: The wardrobe is full of heaps of dead rats!
The wardrobe is full of scorched and broken objects: clothes, tools, and children's toys. Each is labelled with a scrawled number. You don't see anything of value or use.
The wardrobe is full of heaps of bones and incomplete skeletons, each one labelled with a number.

melzar-s-map-piece-searching-bookshelves.text: These books are full of scrawled notes. You open one at a random page...
One excerpt from Melzar's notes is displayed.

melzar-s-map-piece-using-any-key-on-the-.text: The key disintegrates as it unlocks the door.

options.text: Dialogue 1

steps.speaker: Melzar the Mad
steps.text: By the power of custard!

options.text: Dialogue 2

steps.speaker: Melzar the Mad
steps.text: Feel the wrath of my feet!

options.text: Dialogue 3

steps.speaker: Melzar the Mad
steps.text: Let me drink my tea in peace.

options.text: Dialogue 4

steps.speaker: Melzar the Mad
steps.text: Leave me alone, I need to feed my pet rock.

melzar-s-map-piece-searching-the-chest.text: You find a map piece in the chest.

melzar-s-map-piece-studying-melzar-s-map.text: This is a piece of map that you found in Melzar's Maze. You will need to join it to the other two map pieces before you can see the route to Crandor.

options.text: I seek a piece of the map to the island of Crandor.

steps.player: I seek a piece of the map to the island of Crandor.

steps.speaker: Oracle
steps.text: The map's behind a door below, but entering is rather tough. This is what you need to know: You must use the following stuff.

steps.speaker: Oracle
steps.text: First, a drink used by a mage. Next, some worm string, changed to sheet. Then, a small crustacean cage. Last, a bowl that's not seen heat.

options.text: Can you impart your wise knowledge to me, O Oracle?

thalzar-s-map-piece-using-respective-ite.text: You put the silk into the opening in the door.
You put the Lobster pot into the opening in the door.
You put the unfired bowl into the opening in the door.
You pour the Wizard's Mind Bomb into the opening in the door.

thalzar-s-map-piece-searching-the-chest.text: As you open the chest, you notice an inscription on the lid:

Here I rest the map to my beloved home. To whoever finds it, I beg of you, let it be. I was honour-bound not to destroy the map piece, but I have used all my magical skill to keep it from being recovered.

This map leads to the lair of the beast that destroyed my home, devoured my family, and burned to a cinder all that I love. But revenge would not benefit me now, and to disturb this beast is to risk bringing its wrath down upon another land.
I cannot stop you from taking this map piece now, but think on this: if you can slay the Dragon of Crandor, you are a greater hero than my land ever produced. There is no shame in backing out now.
You find a map piece in the chest.

thalzar-s-map-piece-studying-thalzar-s-m.text: This is a piece of map that you found in a secret chest in the Dwarven Mine. You will need to join it to the other two map pieces before you can see the route to Crandor.

options.text: I've heard that one of your number has got hold of part of a map.

steps.player: I've heard that one of your number has got hold of part of a map.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Aha, that'd be Wormbrain.

steps.player: Where would he be?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Wormbrain steals too much. He got caught. Now he lives in Port Sarim town jail.

options.text: So how is life for the goblins?
I believe you've got a piece of map that I need.

steps.player: I believe you've got piece of a map that I need.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: So? Why should I be giving it to you? What you do for Wormbrain?

options.text: I'm not going to do anything for you. Forget it.

steps.player: I'm not going to do anything for you. Forget it.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: Be dat way then.

options.text: I'll let you live. I could just kill you.

steps.player: I'll let you live. I could just kill you.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: Ha! Me in here and you out dere. You not get map piece.

options.text: I suppose I could pay you for the map piece...

steps.player: I suppose I could pay you for the map piece. Say, 500 coins?

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: Me not stoopid, it worth at least 10,000 coins!

options.text: You must be joking! Forget it.

steps.player: You must be joking! Forget it.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: Fine, you not get map piece.

options.text: Alright then, 10,000 it is.

steps.text: If the player does not have enough coins:

steps.player: Alright then, 10,000 coins it is.
Oops, I don't have enough on me.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: Comes back when you has enough.
If the player has enough coins:

steps.player: Alright then, 10,000 coins it is.

steps.text: You buy the map piece from Wormbrain.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: Fank you very much! Now me can bribe da guards, hehehe.

options.text: Where did you get the map piece from?

steps.player: Where did you get the map piece from?

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: We rob house of stupid wizard. She very old, not put up much fight at all. Hahaha!

steps.player: Uh... Hahaha.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: Her house full of pictures of a city on island and old pictures of people. Me not recognise island.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: Me find map piece. Me not know what it is, but it in locked box so me figure it important.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: But, by the time me get box open, other goblins gone. Then me not run fast enough and guards catch me.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: But now you want map piece so must be special! What you do for me to get it?

options.text: What are you in for?

steps.player: What are you in for?

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: Me not sure. Me pick some stuff up and take it away.

steps.player: Well, did the stuff belong to you?

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: Umm...no.

steps.player: Well, that would be why then.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: Oh, right.

options.text: Sorry, thought this was a zoo.

steps.player: Sorry, thought this was a zoo.

lozar-s-map-piece-defeating-wormbrain.text: Wormbrain drops a map piece on the floor.

lozar-s-map-piece-defeating-wormbrain-tr.text: You have already taken Wormbrain's map piece. There is no use in beating him up further.
You have just beaten Wormbrain up. Give the poor goblin a break.

lozar-s-map-piece-studying-lozar-s-map-p.text: This is a piece of map that you got from Wormbrain, the goblin thief. You will need to join it to the other two map pieces before you can see the route to Crandor.

an-old-crandorian-ship-using-a-map-piece.text: You still need one more piece of map.

an-old-crandorian-ship-joining-the-maps-.text: You put the three pieces together and assemble a map that shows the route through the reefs to Crandor.

an-old-crandorian-ship-attempting-to-boa.speaker: Klarense
an-old-crandorian-ship-attempting-to-boa.text: Hey, stay off my ship! That's private property!

an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.speaker: Klarense
an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.text: Hello there! Interested in buying this fine ship? I'm sure I can offer her to you for a much better price than any of those shipwrights ask for!

an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.player: A much better price? What's the catch?

an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.speaker: Klarense
an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.text: Well, she's not quite seaworthy right now...

an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.player: Not seaworthy? Why would I want to buy her then?

an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.speaker: Klarense
an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.text: Because this isn't just any ship! This is the Lady Lumbridge, one of the last Crandorian ships! Despite her size, she's one of the most agile ship around!

an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.speaker: Klarense
an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.text: No, but a bit of work will quickly sort that out!

options.text: I'd like to buy her.

steps.player: I'd like to buy her.

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: Of course! I'm sure the work needed to do on it wouldn't be too expensive.

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: How does 2,000 gold sound? I'll even throw in my cabin boy, Jenkins, for free! He'll swab the decks and splice the mainsails for you!

options.text: Yep, sounds good.

steps.text: If the player does not have enough coins:

steps.player: Yep, sounds good.
...except I don't have that kind of money on me...

steps.text: If the player has enough coins:

steps.player: Yep, sounds good.

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: Okey-dokey! She's all yours!

options.text: I'm not paying that much for a broken boat!

steps.player: I'm not paying that much for a broken boat!

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: That's fair enough, I suppose.

options.text: Why is she damaged?

steps.player: Why is she damaged?

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: Oh, there was no particular accident, just years of wear and tear. It's been a long time since Crandor was destroyed and she's had several owners since then. Unfortunately, not all of them looked after her.

options.text: I think I'll pass.

steps.player: I think I'll pass.

an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.speaker: Klarense
an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-klaren.text: Hello, captain! Here to inspect your new ship? Just a little work and she'll be seaworthy again.

options.text: So, what needs fixing on the ship?

steps.text: If the player has not fixed the ship:

steps.player: So, what needs fixing on this ship?

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: Well, the big gaping hole in the hold is the problem. You'll need a few wooden planks hammered in with steel nails to fix it.
If the player has fixed the ship:

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: I dunno. It looks fine to me.

steps.player: But you said it needed fix-

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: Yes, but that was before you fixed it!

options.text: Would you sail this ship to Crandor for me?

steps.player: So would you like to sail this ship to Crandor for me?

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: Crandor? You're joking, right?

options.text: Yes. Ha ha ha!

steps.player: Yes. Ha ha ha!

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: Crandor's not something we sailors joke about. You can't sail from here to Catherby, or Entrana, or Ardougne without going past that accursed island.

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: You can't get close to it because of the reefs, but you can always see it.

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: Sometimes you can see a dark shape in the sky, circling the island. That's when you have to sail on as quick as you can and pray it's not hungry. Every year, more ships are lost to that dragon.

options.text: No. I want to go to Crandor.

steps.player: No. I want to go to Crandor.

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: Then you must be crazy.

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: That island is surrounded by reefs that would rip this ship to shreds. Even if you found a map, you'd need an experienced captain to stand a chance of getting through

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: and, even if I could get to it, there's no way I'm going any closer to that dragon than I have to. They say it can destroy whole ships with one bite.

options.text: What are you going to do now you don't have a ship?

steps.player: What are you going to do now you don't have a ship?

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: Oh, I'll be fine. I've got work as Port Sarim's first lifeguard!

options.text: Can I board the ship now?

steps.player: Can I board the ship now?

steps.speaker: Klarense
steps.text: Sure thing, she's all yours.

an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-cabin-.speaker: Cabin Boy Jenkins
an-old-crandorian-ship-talking-to-cabin-.text: Ahoy! What d'ye think of yer ship then?

options.text: I'm ready to go back to shore.

steps.player: I'm ready to go back on shore.

steps.text: You disembark from the ship.

options.text: I'd like to inspect her some more.
Can you sail this ship to Crandor?

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.speaker: Sawmill operator
an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.text: Hello there. Are you in need of planks or construction supplies?

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.player: As it so happens, I do need some wooden planks!

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.speaker: Sawmill operator
an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.text: Fortunately for you, you've come to the right place!

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.speaker: Sawmill operator
an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.text: Less fortunately for you, I'm on a legally mandated break right now.

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.player: Could you make an exception? I need the planks to go and fight a dragon.

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.speaker: Sawmill operator
an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.text: A dragon? How are planks going to help you with that?

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.player: I'm repairing a boat to sail to Crandor so that I can slay Elvarg.

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.speaker: Sawmill operator
an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.text: Crandor? Elvarg? Well, far be it from me to stop you trying.

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.player: So you'll make some planks for me?

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.speaker: Sawmill operator
an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.text: I will, but I can't make you too many. It'll be just my luck if King Roald decides to audit this place and I've been making planks off the clock.

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.player: What do you need from me to make some planks?

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.text: If the sawmill operator has already made 9 planks:

steps.speaker: Sawmill operator
steps.text: Unfortunately I can't make any more planks for you without drawing attention to myself. You're going to have to source them elsewhere.

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.speaker: Sawmill operator
an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.text: You'll have to provide the logs and 100 coins for each plank. Just basic logs will do for what you need.

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.speaker: Sawmill operator
an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.text: As a reminder, I can't make you very many without risking an audit, so I'll have to stop at nine planks.
If the player doesn't have any normal logs or coins:

steps.speaker: Sawmill operator
steps.text: You'll need to bring me some more logs.

an-old-crandorian-ship-interacting-with-.text: If the player has logs but not enough coins:

steps.speaker: Sawmill operator
steps.text: Those planks cost 100 coins. You don't have enough money for all of them.

an-old-crandorian-ship-reparing-the-lady.text: If the player does not have any planks:

steps.text: You'll need to use wooden planks on this hole to patch it up.

an-old-crandorian-ship-reparing-the-lady.text: If the player has planks but does not have any steel nails:

steps.text: You need 30 steel nails to attach the plank with.

an-old-crandorian-ship-reparing-the-lady.text: If the player has planks and nails but does not have a hammer:

steps.text: You need a hammer to force the nails in with.
You nail a plank over the hole, but you still need more planks to close the hole completely.
You nail a plank over the hole, but you still need one more plank to close the hole completely.
You nail a final plank over the hole. You have successfully patched the hole in the ship.

options.text: Arrr!
Can you help me get to Crandor Island?

steps.player: Can you help me get to Crandor Island?

steps.speaker: Ahab
steps.text: Arrr, matey, ye canna be serious! That be the home of Elvarg the Dragon!

steps.text: Well, I was a sailor. I've not been able to get work at sea these days, though. They say I'm too old.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Sorry, where was it you said you wanted to go?

steps.text: Crandor?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: But... It would be a chance to sail a ship once more. I'd sail anywhere if it was a chance to sail again.

options.text: Yes

steps.player: Yes!

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Well, you're a braver man than I!

steps.player: Why is everyone so scared of this dragon?

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Back in my father's day, Crandor was an important city-state. Politically, it was as important as Falador or Varrock and its ships traded with every port.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: But, one day when I was little, all contact was lost. The trading ships and the diplomatic envoys just stopped coming.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I remember my father being very scared. He posted lookouts on the roof to warn if the dragon was approaching. All the city rulers were worried that Elvarg would devastate the whole continent.

options.text: I'd better leave that dragon alone.

steps.player: I'd better leave that dragon alone.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: That's a relief. I would hate to see such a promising adventurer cut down in [his/her/their] prime.

options.text: So, are you going to give me the shield or not?

options.text: No
